identity.name: Watson Brake culture
alt_names: Middle Archaic mound builders of the Ouachita valley

correction.text: "in the floodplain of the Ouachita River, near present-day Monroe in northern Louisiana"; "eleven earthwork mounds"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. "The analysis of 27 radiocarbon dates indicates that the site was initially occupied around 4000 BCE"; "Mound construction began at approximately 3500 BCE, and continued for approximately 500 years"; "The site appears to have been abandoned around 2800 BCE". One 80 km disc round Monroe (75 land cells) stands for the Ouachita floodplain: the page describes one site of eleven mounds in an oval "nearly 900 feet across", and mentions other Middle Archaic sites in Louisiana and Florida without naming them.

region.text: "in the floodplain of the Ouachita River, near present-day Monroe in northern Louisiana"; "eleven earthwork mounds"

ledger.note: 4000 BCE: hunter-gatherers first occupy the Watson Brake site on the Ouachita River, Louisiana. "The analysis of 27 radiocarbon dates indicates that the site was initially occupied around 4000 BCE." The year is the page's; the disc round Monroe is the dossier's stand-in for the site's surroundings.

3500 BCE: mound building begins at Watson Brake. Infobox "Built: 3500 BCE"; "Mound construction began at approximately 3500 BCE, and continued for approximately 500 years"; the Archaic-period page agrees: "organized to build monumental earthwork mound complexes as early as 3500 BC".

region.text: "in the floodplain of the Ouachita River, near present-day Monroe in northern Louisiana"; "eleven earthwork mounds"

ledger.note: 2800 BCE: Watson Brake is abandoned. "The site appears to have been abandoned around 2800 BCE." The next mound-building culture, Poverty Point, is "begun about 1500 BCE", so the valley passes to nobody for 1,300 years.

certainty.note: One site cluster; no border is recorded.

sources.title: Watson Brake
sources.note: Occupied c. 4000 BCE, mounds from c. 3500 BCE, abandoned c. 2800 BCE; Ouachita floodplain near Monroe, Louisiana; eleven mounds; Poverty Point begun c. 1500 BCE.

sources.title: Archaic period (North America)
sources.note: Archaic 8000-1000 BC; Middle Archaic mounds from 3500 BC; Old Copper complex 4000-1000 BC; Oshara 5500 BC-500 AD; Cochise.

notes: Watson Brake and the Middle Archaic mound builders of northern Louisiana. The page describes a single site; the culture as a whole (Middle Archaic mound sites in northern Louisiana, Mississippi and Florida, Archaic-period page: "Since the 1990s, secure dating of multiple Middle Archaic sites in northern Louisiana, Mississippi and Florida") is not dated site by site on either page, so only the Monroe disc is drawn. The brief's Eastern Woodlands Archaic is otherwise blank: the Shell Mound Archaic page did not load (Shell_Mound_Archaic, URL_NOT_FOUND) and the Archaic-period page gives only "starting around 4000 BC, people exploited wetland resources" and shell rings 3000-1000 BC for the Southeast. Poverty Point (c. 1500 BCE) has no dossier in this batch.
